pathway.title: OPEN TEXT CORP — Credit Snapshot
pathway.question: Should we own this issuer, in which instrument, and why?

runs.text: OPEN TEXT CORP has de-levered through divestiture proceeds and cash: debt principal fell from USD 6,485,375 thousand at June 30, 2025 to USD 5,836,525 thousand at June 30, 2026 and USD 5,827,563 thousand at September 30, 2026, taking total debt to adjusted EBITDA from 3.63x to 3.07x and then 3.10x on a last-twelve-months basis, and net debt to 2.58x [financial base]. Documentary Fact. The mechanism matters: part of the repayment came from selling businesses that also carried earnings, so the ratio improvement is real but partly bought with a smaller EBITDA base [business context timeline].

The interest burden has fallen sharply, from cash interest paid of USD 533,866 thousand in FY2024 to USD 300,111 thousand on a last-twelve-months basis, lifting adjusted EBITDA to cash interest from 3.69x to 6.26x [financial base]. Documentary Fact. Lower interest leaves more of each dollar of EBITDA to reach free cash flow, which was USD 844,805 thousand on a last-twelve-months basis, and gives earnings room to fall before debt service is strained. The cover uses issuer-defined adjusted EBITDA, which adds back share-based compensation and special charges that have recurred in each of the last three years (USD 135,305 thousand in FY2024, USD 145,890 thousand in FY2025 and USD 133,020 thousand in FY2026) [financial base], so cover on a stricter definition would be lower. Analyst Interpretation.

The covenant position is wide on the printed values: the calculated net leverage ratio was 3.35, 3.02 and 2.75 at December 2025, March 2026 and June 2026 against a maximum of 4.50 [financial base]. Documentary Fact. The September 30, 2026 value is not printed in the filing; management states 2.55x without a definition, and that statement stays attributed [financial base]. Management Language. Headroom of 1.75 turns at June 2026 means a maintenance breach is unlikely to be the first point of stress; the likelier constraint is cash flow used for distributions.

Recurring revenue gives visibility but the trend is negative: recurring revenue is 84.1 percent of Q1 FY2027 revenue, support revenue fell 9.0 percent and license 8.0 percent, while cloud grew 4.3 percent, and the cloud net renewal rate eased to 95 percent from 96 percent [business context]. Documentary Fact. Support is the largest revenue line and is annual-renewal, so attrition hits the highest-margin contracted base first; cloud growth is replacing it at a lower margin. Total revenue was down 4.0 percent year on year in Q1 FY2027 [financial base], partly from the eDOCS and Vertica sales.

Management's FY2027 outlook is below the last twelve months: revenue USD 5,135 to 5,185 million, adjusted EBITDA margin 32 to 33 percent and free cash flow USD 625 to 725 million, which implies adjusted EBITDA of about USD 1,643.2 to 1,711.1 million against USD 1,878,183 thousand on a last-twelve-months basis [business context]. Management Language, qualified. If met, and with principal unchanged at USD 5,527,563 thousand after the October 2026 events, total debt to adjusted EBITDA would rise to about 3.23x to 3.36x (calculation 1). Analyst Interpretation. The outlook is a management statement and can be revised after the enterprise assessment.

The October 2026 refinancing extended the maturity profile but made the structure more secured. USD 500 million of 6.70 percent secured notes due 2031 and USD 500 million of 7.15 percent secured notes due 2033 replaced the USD 1,000 million 6.90 percent secured notes due 2027, USD 300 million of the 2028 notes were bought back and the USD 750.0 million revolver was extended to October 2031 [financial base; business context]. Documentary Fact. The nearest note maturity moves to February 2028 (USD 600.0 million), but the secured share of principal rises from 43.4 percent to 45.7 percent because unsecured notes were retired, so unsecured creditors rank behind a larger secured pool, while the annual cash coupon on the exchanged notes falls by USD 11,375 thousand. Cash used for the tender, the premium and costs are not supplied, so post-October liquidity is lower than the USD 983.3 million of cash at September 30, 2026 by an amount that cannot be stated.

Shareholder returns absorb most of the free cash flow: dividends and repurchases were USD 737,669 thousand in FY2026, 91.4 percent of USD 807,517 thousand of free cash flow [financial base]. Documentary Fact. The company is widely held, with the largest holder at 11.17 percent and no sponsor, so no sponsor extraction is documented [business context]. Documentary Fact. The distribution policy is a Board choice, and the dividend is subject to credit agreement limits whose terms are not in the pack, so how far the Board can keep distributing if earnings fall cannot be measured. Insufficient Information.

runs.text: Strengths. (1) Deleveraging and cover: total debt to adjusted EBITDA of 3.10x and cash interest cover of 6.26x on a last-twelve-months basis give room for earnings to fall; basis: financial base. Documentary Fact. (2) Recurring revenue and diversification: an 84.1 percent recurring share, no customer above 10 percent of receivables, no country other than the United States above 10 percent of revenue and a single reported segment spread across product categories reduce concentration; basis: business context. Documentary Fact. (3) Liquidity and maturities: USD 983.3 million of cash plus an undrawn USD 750.0 million revolver at September 30, 2026, before any letters of credit, a revolver extended to October 2031 and no note maturing before February 2028; basis: financial base. Documentary Fact. (4) Cash generation: USD 844,805 thousand of last-twelve-months free cash flow, up in Q1 FY2027 to USD 138,517 thousand from USD 101,229 thousand; basis: financial base. Documentary Fact. (5) Ownership: dispersed institutional holders and no sponsor remove the sponsor-extraction mechanic; basis: business context. Documentary Fact. (6) Covenant headroom of 1.75 turns at June 2026 on the printed ratio; basis: financial base. Documentary Fact.

Weaknesses. (1) Shrinking base: revenue down 4.0 percent in Q1 FY2027, support down 9.0 percent, license down 8.0 percent, cloud net renewal rate down to 95 percent; basis: financial base and business context. Documentary Fact. (2) Guided step-down: the FY2027 outlook implies lower adjusted EBITDA and free cash flow than the last twelve months; basis: business context. Management Language, qualified. (3) Earnings quality: adjusted EBITDA relies on add-backs, including special charges that recur every year; basis: financial base. Analyst Interpretation. (4) Distribution intensity: 91.4 percent of FY2026 free cash flow returned to shareholders, leaving debt reduction that in FY2026 was partly funded by divestiture proceeds; basis: financial base. Analyst Interpretation. (5) Structure and cost: a larger secured share and higher coupons on the replacement notes; basis: financial base. Documentary Fact. (6) Contingent and unmeasured claims: the Canada Revenue Agency matter, which the filing sizes at approximately USD 88.8 million for fiscal 2012 to 2016 and up to approximately USD 470 million of deferred tax assets for fiscal 2017 to 2021 with no accrual, sits outside debt; letters of credit, guarantor structure, ratings and post-October cash are not supplied; basis: financial base. Documentary Fact for the amounts; Insufficient Information for the unmeasured items. (7) Leadership and strategy in flux: the chief executive and chief financial officer both changed within FY2026 and an enterprise assessment may change portfolio and reporting; basis: business context. Documentary Fact.

runs.text: The transaction that matters for the creditor is the October 2026 refinancing, a closed subsequent event after the September 30, 2026 balance sheet and inside the cutoff. Type: a refinancing and partial liability management. Parties: the registrant as issuer, guaranteed on a senior secured basis by certain subsidiaries; the initial purchasers, trustees and holders tendering are not named in the pack. Sponsor: none. On October 1, 2026 the company issued two series of senior secured notes: [10-Q-Sep26 page:43 — "On October 1, 2026, the Company issued $500 million in aggregate principal amount of 6.70% senior secured notes due 2031"] and a second 500 million series at 7.15 percent due 2033, both paying interest semi-annually from April 15, 2027 and maturing on October 15, 2031 and October 15, 2033 respectively. Debt raised is therefore 1,000 million of new secured notes, secured with the same priority as the senior credit facilities [10-Q-Sep26 page:44 — "are secured with the same priority as the Company’s senior credit facilities"] and structurally subordinated to liabilities of subsidiaries that do not guarantee them. Use of proceeds: on October 2, 2026 the proceeds, together with cash on hand, funded the redemption in full of the 1.0 billion 6.90 percent senior secured notes due 2027 including the redemption premium, accrued interest and costs, and the cash purchase and cancellation of 300.0 million of the 3.875 percent senior notes due 2028 [10-Q-Sep26 page:44 — "On October 2, 2026, the Company purchased and cancelled $300.0 million of the aggregate outstanding principal amount of the Senior Notes 2028"]. The revolving credit facility of 750.0 million, undrawn at September 30, 2026, was amended on October 1, 2026 to extend its maturity from December 19, 2028 to October 1, 2031, subject to certain conditions, and its borrowings rank pari passu with the term loan and the new secured notes.

Effect on the credit, as the financial base handoff computes it: principal debt falls from 5,827,563 to 5,527,563 (US$ thousands); the nearest note maturity moves from December 1, 2027 to February 15, 2028 and falls from 1,900,000 across the two near notes to 600,000 for the remaining 2028 notes; new maturities of 500,000 fall in fiscal 2032 and 500,000 in fiscal 2034; secured principal stays at 2,527,563 while its share of the total rises from 43.4 percent to 45.7 percent; and the annual cash coupon on the exchanged notes falls by 11,375 before premium and fees. The cost side is not quantified in the pack: the redemption premium, the tender price and the cash used are not stated, so the liquidity effect is a reduction of cash on hand by an amount that is not supplied. The management characterisation is that the transactions provide greater financial flexibility [PR-Nov26 page:1 — "providing the Company with greater financial flexibility"], which is Management Language and is not adopted; the documented facts are a longer maturity profile, a higher secured share and coupons of 6.70 and 7.15 percent against 6.90 percent on the retired secured notes. Status: closed. New debt issues in the pack: only these two series; there are no pending or committed financings, no acquisition financing and no dividend recapitalisation.

Earlier transactions that shape the structure: the 2023 Micro Focus acquisition for 6.2 billion, for which the term loan and the 2027 secured notes were raised; the 2024 AMC sale for 2.275 billion, which funded a term loan prepayment of 1.31 billion in FY2024 together with cash on hand; and the eDOCS and Vertica sales in FY2026 for 163.0 million and 150.0 million, each applied to prepay the term loan. These sales removed revenue and earnings while reducing debt, which is why the divestiture comparability break is carried in every period comparison. A further dividend of $0.28 per share was declared on November 3, 2026, payable December 18, 2026; it is a future term, not an executed payment.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: For OPEN TEXT CORP the financial base shows a credit that has de-levered and cut interest cost while its top line contracts. Gross debt principal at June 30, 2026 was below June 30, 2025 by the amount of repayments in FY2026, funded by divestiture proceeds and cash on hand, and debt at September 30, 2026 was almost unchanged from June 30, 2026. Against adjusted EBITDA, total debt fell from 3.63x at FY2025 to 3.07x at FY2026 and was 3.10x on a last-twelve-months basis at September 30, 2026; EBITDA to cash interest paid rose from 3.69x in FY2024 to 5.92x in FY2026 and 6.26x on the last-twelve-months basis. The calculated covenant ratio printed in the filings fell from 3.35 at December 31, 2025 to 2.75 at June 30, 2026 against a 4.50 maximum, so maintenance headroom is large on the printed figures. The pressure points are the contracting revenue base (Q1 FY2027 revenue down year on year, with client support and license lines falling while cloud grew), the divestitures that removed earnings together with debt, the heavy shareholder distributions in FY2026 relative to free cash flow, an unquantified Canada Revenue Agency tax dispute, and the October 2026 refinancing that lengthened maturities but swapped 6.90% secured notes due 2027 for 6.70% and 7.15% secured notes due 2031 and 2033, raising the secured debt share. The view is bounded by three missing inputs: covenant EBITDA, letters of credit that may reduce revolver availability, and cash after the October 2026 transactions.

fields.value: The revolver and the term loan both carry a maintenance test [10-Q-Sep26 page:19 — "we must maintain a “consolidated net leverage” ratio of no more than 4.50:1.00 at the end of each financial quarter"]. The ratio is defined with debt reduced by unrestricted cash, including guarantees and letters of credit, over trailing twelve months earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation, amortization, restructuring, share-based compensation and other miscellaneous charges. The printed values are: [10-Q-Dec25 page:23 — "as calculated in accordance with the applicable agreement, was 3.35:1:00"], [10-Q-Mar26 page:24 — "as calculated in accordance with the applicable agreement, was 3.02:1:00"] and [10-K page:124 — "as calculated in accordance with the applicable agreement, was 2.75:1.00"]. For September 30, 2026 the 10-Q states [10-Q-Sep26 page:21 — "As of September 30, 2026, we are in compliance with our consolidated net leverage ratio covenant."] and the earnings release gives a management statement [PR-Nov26 page:3 — "Our net leverage ratio is 2.55x as of September 30, 2026."] with no definition or inputs.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: For OPEN TEXT CORP the business is a diversified, global enterprise software and cybersecurity vendor whose revenue is dominated by annual-renewal client support and cloud subscriptions, which gives good revenue visibility but a base that fell in the latest quarter, with the support and license lines declining and growth concentrated in cloud lines. The registrant is a widely held listed company with no sponsor and no holder above about eleven percent, so the creditor risk is not sponsor extraction; it is a management and Board capital allocation choice between debt reduction, a quarterly dividend and share repurchases, taken in a year of leadership change and a strategic enterprise assessment whose conclusions are scheduled for an investor day in February 2027. The credit-relevant history is acquisition-led: the 2023 Micro Focus acquisition created the debt load, the 2024 AMC sale and the 2026 eDOCS and Vertica sales repaid part of it at the cost of earnings, and the October 2026 refinancing replaced the 2027 secured notes and part of the 2028 notes with secured notes due 2031 and 2033, which extends the maturity wall but raises the share of secured debt and the coupon on the replaced paper. Management's FY2027 outlook, a management statement, points to a lower margin and lower free cash flow than the last twelve months, which is the main forward uncertainty. Evidence is primary and dated for facts and management-only for outlook and strategy; no customer-level, rating or executed-document evidence is available.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The transaction that matters for the creditor is the October 2026 refinancing, a closed subsequent event after the September 30, 2026 balance sheet and inside the cutoff. Type: a refinancing and partial liability management. Parties: the registrant as issuer, guaranteed on a senior secured basis by certain subsidiaries; the initial purchasers, trustees and holders tendering are not named in the pack. Sponsor: none. On October 1, 2026 the company issued two series of senior secured notes: [10-Q-Sep26 page:43 — "On October 1, 2026, the Company issued $500 million in aggregate principal amount of 6.70% senior secured notes due 2031"] and a second 500 million series at 7.15 percent due 2033, both paying interest semi-annually from April 15, 2027 and maturing on October 15, 2031 and October 15, 2033 respectively. Debt raised is therefore 1,000 million of new secured notes, secured with the same priority as the senior credit facilities [10-Q-Sep26 page:44 — "are secured with the same priority as the Company’s senior credit facilities"] and structurally subordinated to liabilities of subsidiaries that do not guarantee them. Use of proceeds: on October 2, 2026 the proceeds, together with cash on hand, funded the redemption in full of the 1.0 billion 6.90 percent senior secured notes due 2027 including the redemption premium, accrued interest and costs, and the cash purchase and cancellation of 300.0 million of the 3.875 percent senior notes due 2028 [10-Q-Sep26 page:44 — "On October 2, 2026, the Company purchased and cancelled $300.0 million of the aggregate outstanding principal amount of the Senior Notes 2028"]. The revolving credit facility of 750.0 million, undrawn at September 30, 2026, was amended on October 1, 2026 to extend its maturity from December 19, 2028 to October 1, 2031, subject to certain conditions, and its borrowings rank pari passu with the term loan and the new secured notes.

The cost side is not quantified in the pack: the redemption premium, the tender price and the cash used are not stated, so the liquidity effect is a reduction of cash on hand by an amount that is not supplied. The management characterisation is that the transactions provide greater financial flexibility [PR-Nov26 page:1 — "providing the Company with greater financial flexibility"], which is Management Language and is not adopted; the documented facts are a longer maturity profile, a higher secured share and coupons of 6.70 and 7.15 percent against 6.90 percent on the retired secured notes. Status: closed. New debt issues in the pack: only these two series; there are no pending or committed financings, no acquisition financing and no dividend recapitalisation.

These sales removed revenue and earnings while reducing debt, which is why the divestiture comparability break is carried in every period comparison. A further dividend of $0.28 per share was declared on November 3, 2026, payable December 18, 2026; it is a future term, not an executed payment.

The financial base handoff shows that shareholder distributions in FY2026 were 91.4 percent of free cash flow, in the same year that debt principal fell by 648,850. fields.value: OPEN TEXT CORP has de-levered through divestiture proceeds and cash: debt principal fell from USD 6,485,375 thousand at June 30, 2025 to USD 5,836,525 thousand at June 30, 2026 and USD 5,827,563 thousand at September 30, 2026, taking total debt to adjusted EBITDA from 3.63x to 3.07x and then 3.10x on a last-twelve-months basis, and net debt to 2.58x [financial base]. Documentary Fact. The mechanism matters: part of the repayment came from selling businesses that also carried earnings, so the ratio improvement is real but partly bought with a smaller EBITDA base [business context timeline].

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The interest burden has fallen sharply, from cash interest paid of USD 533,866 thousand in FY2024 to USD 300,111 thousand on a last-twelve-months basis, lifting adjusted EBITDA to cash interest from 3.69x to 6.26x [financial base]. Documentary Fact. Lower interest leaves more of each dollar of EBITDA to reach free cash flow, which was USD 844,805 thousand on a last-twelve-months basis, and gives earnings room to fall before debt service is strained. The cover uses issuer-defined adjusted EBITDA, which adds back share-based compensation and special charges that have recurred in each of the last three years (USD 135,305 thousand in FY2024, USD 145,890 thousand in FY2025 and USD 133,020 thousand in FY2026) [financial base], so cover on a stricter definition would be lower. Analyst Interpretation.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The covenant position is wide on the printed values: the calculated net leverage ratio was 3.35, 3.02 and 2.75 at December 2025, March 2026 and June 2026 against a maximum of 4.50 [financial base]. Documentary Fact. The September 30, 2026 value is not printed in the filing; management states 2.55x without a definition, and that statement stays attributed [financial base]. Management Language. Headroom of 1.75 turns at June 2026 means a maintenance breach is unlikely to be the first point of stress; the likelier constraint is cash flow used for distributions.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Recurring revenue gives visibility but the trend is negative: recurring revenue is 84.1 percent of Q1 FY2027 revenue, support revenue fell 9.0 percent and license 8.0 percent, while cloud grew 4.3 percent, and the cloud net renewal rate eased to 95 percent from 96 percent [business context]. Documentary Fact. Support is the largest revenue line and is annual-renewal, so attrition hits the highest-margin contracted base first; cloud growth is replacing it at a lower margin. Total revenue was down 4.0 percent year on year in Q1 FY2027 [financial base], partly from the eDOCS and Vertica sales.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Management's FY2027 outlook is below the last twelve months: revenue USD 5,135 to 5,185 million, adjusted EBITDA margin 32 to 33 percent and free cash flow USD 625 to 725 million, which implies adjusted EBITDA of about USD 1,643.2 to 1,711.1 million against USD 1,878,183 thousand on a last-twelve-months basis [business context]. Management Language, qualified. If met, and with principal unchanged at USD 5,527,563 thousand after the October 2026 events, total debt to adjusted EBITDA would rise to about 3.23x to 3.36x (calculation 1). Analyst Interpretation. The outlook is a management statement and can be revised after the enterprise assessment.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The October 2026 refinancing extended the maturity profile but made the structure more secured. USD 500 million of 6.70 percent secured notes due 2031 and USD 500 million of 7.15 percent secured notes due 2033 replaced the USD 1,000 million 6.90 percent secured notes due 2027, USD 300 million of the 2028 notes were bought back and the USD 750.0 million revolver was extended to October 2031 [financial base; business context]. Documentary Fact. The nearest note maturity moves to February 2028 (USD 600.0 million), but the secured share of principal rises from 43.4 percent to 45.7 percent because unsecured notes were retired, so unsecured creditors rank behind a larger secured pool, while the annual cash coupon on the exchanged notes falls by USD 11,375 thousand. Cash used for the tender, the premium and costs are not supplied, so post-October liquidity is lower than the USD 983.3 million of cash at September 30, 2026 by an amount that cannot be stated.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Shareholder returns absorb most of the free cash flow: dividends and repurchases were USD 737,669 thousand in FY2026, 91.4 percent of USD 807,517 thousand of free cash flow [financial base]. Documentary Fact. The company is widely held, with the largest holder at 11.17 percent and no sponsor, so no sponsor extraction is documented [business context]. Documentary Fact. The distribution policy is a Board choice, and the dividend is subject to credit agreement limits whose terms are not in the pack, so how far the Board can keep distributing if earnings fall cannot be measured. Insufficient Information.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Strengths. (1) Deleveraging and cover: total debt to adjusted EBITDA of 3.10x and cash interest cover of 6.26x on a last-twelve-months basis give room for earnings to fall; basis: financial base. Documentary Fact. (2) Recurring revenue and diversification: an 84.1 percent recurring share, no customer above 10 percent of receivables, no country other than the United States above 10 percent of revenue and a single reported segment spread across product categories reduce concentration; basis: business context. Documentary Fact. (3) Liquidity and maturities: USD 983.3 million of cash plus an undrawn USD 750.0 million revolver at September 30, 2026, before any letters of credit, a revolver extended to October 2031 and no note maturing before February 2028; basis: financial base. Documentary Fact. (4) Cash generation: USD 844,805 thousand of last-twelve-months free cash flow, up in Q1 FY2027 to USD 138,517 thousand from USD 101,229 thousand; basis: financial base. Documentary Fact. (5) Ownership: dispersed institutional holders and no sponsor remove the sponsor-extraction mechanic; basis: business context. Documentary Fact. (6) Covenant headroom of 1.75 turns at June 2026 on the printed ratio; basis: financial base. Documentary Fact.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Weaknesses. (1) Shrinking base: revenue down 4.0 percent in Q1 FY2027, support down 9.0 percent, license down 8.0 percent, cloud net renewal rate down to 95 percent; basis: financial base and business context. Documentary Fact. (2) Guided step-down: the FY2027 outlook implies lower adjusted EBITDA and free cash flow than the last twelve months; basis: business context. Management Language, qualified. (3) Earnings quality: adjusted EBITDA relies on add-backs, including special charges that recur every year; basis: financial base. Analyst Interpretation. (4) Distribution intensity: 91.4 percent of FY2026 free cash flow returned to shareholders, leaving debt reduction that in FY2026 was partly funded by divestiture proceeds; basis: financial base. Analyst Interpretation. (5) Structure and cost: a larger secured share and higher coupons on the replacement notes; basis: financial base. Documentary Fact. (6) Contingent and unmeasured claims: the Canada Revenue Agency matter, which the filing sizes at approximately USD 88.8 million for fiscal 2012 to 2016 and up to approximately USD 470 million of deferred tax assets for fiscal 2017 to 2021 with no accrual, sits outside debt; letters of credit, guarantor structure, ratings and post-October cash are not supplied; basis: financial base. Documentary Fact for the amounts; Insufficient Information for the unmeasured items. (7) Leadership and strategy in flux: the chief executive and chief financial officer both changed within FY2026 and an enterprise assessment may change portfolio and reporting; basis: business context. Documentary Fact.

fields.value: 1. Illustrative leverage if the FY2027 outlook is met, with principal unchanged: pro forma principal USD 5,527.563 million divided by outlook-implied adjusted EBITDA of USD 1,711.1 million is 3.23x; divided by USD 1,643.2 million is 3.36x. Inputs from the financial base (principal 5,527,563 thousand) and the business context (outlook-implied EBITDA range 1,643.2 to 1,711.1 million). This ignores scheduled amortization and any further repayment, and uses gross principal because post-October cash is not supplied; it is a scenario, not a forecast.

fields.name: Quote

Free cash flow after an annualized dividend at the Q1 FY2027 rate: dividends of USD 66.5 million in Q1 FY2027 times four is USD 266.0 million, which is 42.6 percent of the low end (USD 625 million) and 36.7 percent of the high end (USD 725 million) of guided free cash flow. Inputs: business context outlook range; dividend paid in Q1 FY2027 as stated in the financial base. Illustrative only; repurchases are excluded and discretionary.
